cells.tense: Right now you are standing where feeling with someone has become plain work, and it holds.
cells.act: rest in the balance you already have
cells.ask: Add nothing to how you and someone close to you are doing. Take the connection as it stands and rest in it.
cells.core:
This part of you is holding. You can sit with someone and feel it from inside their side without losing your own footing, and you can hold the fact that the two of you see something differently without needing to close the gap tonight. That is why people stay near you. What they meet reads as ease rather than effort, and it is not ease; it is a steadiness that keeps itself, running quietly underneath.

What this balance is free to feed next is rest, and rest is offered, not owed. Add nothing to how you and someone close to you are doing. Take the connection as it stands. You will find it holds without your hand on it. If something surfaces, let it keep until morning the way you would let a sleeper sleep. Nothing needs deciding before then.
cells.sheetLine: The connection is already steady. Let it hold without you.
cells.verb: walking on from what was gathered toward the connection that asks for you
cells.place: where two people try to feel with each other and not only about each other

cells.tense: You are already living past a goodbye that has not happened yet, and the people near you can feel the distance.
cells.act: start building where the false thing fell
cells.ask: Put an hour into something you and another person are actually keeping — not a farewell, not what follows after — and build only that.
cells.core:
Somewhere in your head it is already over. You have rehearsed the walk away, the explanation, the life that comes afterward, and the rehearsal runs while the real connection is still here. People feel it as you being partly gone. You feel it as being careful. The leaving has gotten ahead of anything it could be following.

Start building where the false thing fell. Put an hour into something you and another person are actually keeping — not a farewell, not what follows after — and build only that. One shared thing, made smaller than it was, made real. If the goodbye is truly coming, an hour will not stop it. It only means you were present for the part that still exists. Whatever you make may look plain. Let it look plain.

cells.tense: The door you already walked through is still the one you stand at, and nobody is on the far side with you.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Set down one feeling you keep having about a relationship, and write what follows from it and what you add yourself.
cells.core:
You made the crossing and you are still on the far side of it alone. Something in how you are with people closed down, and you can feel the distance without being able to say when it opened. Warmth is still something you offer; you just do not expect it to land, and you have stopped arranging your days around anyone. You are not cold. You are braced, and the brace is old enough to feel like your personality.

Set down one feeling you keep having about a relationship, and write what follows from it and what you add yourself. Two columns on a single page: what happened, and what you decided it meant. One relationship, one sitting. The point is not to fix the connection. The point is to see the logic you have been running, which has been running you, and to be the one reading it.

cells.tense: You keep a connection alive by hand most weeks and file it under nothing at all.
cells.ask: When you catch yourself smoothing something over for someone, leave the moment alone and keep your hands off it a while.
cells.core:
You are the one who notices when somebody is being left out and moves the conversation their way. You adjust what you say so it lands, you remember what a person mentioned last month and bring it up again, you make the gathering feel easy. Asked about it, you would tell anyone you just like people. The weaving going on there is your work, and you do not count it as work.

When you catch yourself smoothing something over for someone, leave the moment alone and keep your hands off it a while. You do not have to let the awkward thing stand; you only have to know you were the one holding the gathering before you pick it up again. That is the whole difference between a person who is warm and a person managing warmth. One of them knows whose effort it was.
